target: Мы ждём автобус уже двадцать минут.
english: We've been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
tip: For an action still going on, Russian uses the present with уже (uzhe = already): ждём уже двадцать минут (zhdyom uzhe dvadtsat minut = have been waiting twenty minutes).

target: Я знаю этого человека очень давно.
english: I've known this person for a very long time.
tip: Animate masculine accusative copies the genitive form: этого человека (etogo cheloveka = this person), because a person is the object, not этот человек (etot chelovek).

target: Они переехали в Москву пять лет назад.
english: They moved to Moscow five years ago.
tip: назад (nazad = ago) comes after the time span, not before it: пять лет назад (pyat let nazad = five years ago).

english: The roof of the house is covered with snow.
tip: covered with uses the instrumental with no preposition: покрыта снегом (pokryta snegom = covered with snow), no separate word for with.

english: Congratulations on your promotion!
tip: Поздравляю (pozdravlyayu = congratulations) takes с plus the instrumental: с повышением (s povysheniyem = on the promotion).

english: The eighth of March is International Women's Day.
tip: Dates put day and month in the genitive: Восьмого марта (Vosmogo marta = the eighth of March), literally of-the-eighth of-March.

english: She took the children home.
tip: Домой (domoy = homeward) already means 'to home', so it needs no preposition and no case change.

english: He put the book on the table.
tip: Motion onto a surface takes на plus accusative: на стол (na stol = onto the table). Resting on it would be на столе (na stole).

target: Мне очень жаль, что так случилось.
english: I am really sorry about what happened.
tip: Мне жаль (mne zhal = I'm sorry) uses a dative person plus жаль, with no verb for 'to be'.

english: Grandmother will soon help a friend.
tip: The verb поможет (pomozhet = will help) takes a dative object, so друг (drug) becomes другу (drugu = to a friend).

english: Good luck with your exams!
tip: Wishing someone something uses genitive: Удачи (udachi = good luck), a shortened form of 'I wish you luck'.

english: The concert will start in an hour.
tip: Через (cherez = in) plus accusative sets a time from now: Через час (cherez chas = in an hour).

english: She dreams about a beautiful house.
tip: The verb мечтает (mechtaet = dreams) takes о plus prepositional: о красивом доме (o krasivom dome = about a beautiful house).

english: A young couple walks along the embankment.
tip: По (po = along) plus dative traces movement over a surface: по набережной (po naberezhnoy = along the embankment).

english: Part of the money went to repairs.
tip: Part-words take the genitive: часть денег (chast' deneg = part of the money), and ушла (ushla) agrees feminine with часть.

english: I need to buy a kilogram of apples.
tip: After a quantity word the counted noun goes genitive plural: килограмм яблок (kilogramm yablok = a kilo of apples).

target: Красивые цветы растут в нашем саду.
english: Beautiful flowers grow in our garden.
tip: Some masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the location case: саду (sadu = in the garden), from сад (sad), not саде (sade).

target: Он открыл тяжёлую дверь и вошёл.
english: He opened the heavy door and entered.
tip: The prefix в- (v-) adds inward motion: вошёл (voshyol = went in), while plain шёл (shyol) just means was walking.

target: Конечно, я помогу вам с удовольствием!
english: Of course, I will help you with pleasure!
tip: С (s = with) plus instrumental gives manner here: с удовольствием (s udovolstviem = with pleasure, gladly).

target: Продавец иногда играет в шахматы в парке.
english: The salesman sometimes plays chess in the park.
tip: The verb играет (igraet = plays) takes в plus accusative for games: в шахматы (v shakhmaty = chess).

target: Здравствуйте, мы с вами уже встречались на конференции.
english: Hello, we already met at the conference.
tip: встречались (vstrechalis = met) ends in a reflexive -сь (-s), which with a plural subject reads as reciprocal: they met each other.

english: Have a good flight!
tip: Russian good wishes use the genitive: Хорошего полёта (Khoroshego polyota = of a good flight), literally wishing you 'of a good flight'.

english: I need your help.
tip: нужна (nuzhna = needed) agrees with the thing needed, not the person: помощь (pomoshch = help) is feminine, so нужна, not нужен.

english: The bus pulled up to the stop.
tip: к (k) means toward and takes the dative: к остановке (k ostanovke = up to the stop). Use it for approaching a point.

english: Friends liked our new house.
tip: With понравился (ponravilsya = was liked), the liker goes dative, Друзьям (Druzyam = to friends), and the verb agrees with the thing liked, дом (dom = house).

english: The food is delicious at this restaurant.
tip: вкусно готовят (vkusno gotovyat) has no subject, meaning 'people cook deliciously'; subjectless 'they' becomes an English passive: the food is delicious.

english: We are going to the park for a walk.
tip: идём (idyom = we go) is for going on foot; ехать (yekhat = go by vehicle) is for vehicles. Russian marks how you travel, English uses 'go' for both.

english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
tip: Быть (byt) has no present-tense form, but its future is regular: всё будет хорошо (vsyo budet khorosho = all will be fine).

english: Several students were late for the lecture.
tip: несколько (neskolko = several) takes the genitive plural: несколько студентов (studentov = of students). Quantity words govern the genitive.

english: How do you say this word in Russian?
tip: по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is how you name a language of speech: по- plus the adverb, hyphenated and lowercase, never capitalized.
